Optional PDF writer

Krilla 0.8.2 (https://github.com/LaurenzV/krilla), MIT OR Apache-2.0.
Upstream licence texts are retained in licenses/pdf-writer.
The optional writer embeds Compact ICC Profiles by Clinton Ingram
(https://github.com/saucecontrol/Compact-ICC-Profiles), under CC0-1.0.
See licenses/pdf-writer/LICENSE-ICC.txt and ATTRIBUTION.md for sources and hashes.
The writer adds no font files. Its four existing ICC profiles are retained under vendor/krilla/icc.

Krilla is vendored with a native unwind-cleanup patch; see vendor/krilla/README.craft.md
and vendor/krilla/SOURCE.json. Its upstream MIT/Apache-2.0 licences and CC0 profiles are unchanged.

Optional PDF reader

Hayro 0.7.1, hayro-interpret 0.7.0, hayro-syntax 0.7.2 and hayro-jbig2 0.3.0
(https://github.com/LaurenzV/hayro), MIT OR Apache-2.0, retain their upstream licence files.
These patched sources are transferred from PdfCraft revision
7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a (https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft).
See vendor/README.craft-reader.md and each crate's SOURCE.json for provenance and local changes.
The reader retains the existing Foxit/PDFium standard-14 font assets (BSD-3-Clause),
Compact ICC Profiles by Clinton Ingram (CC0-1.0), and dependency CMaps (BSD-3-Clause).
Their licences and per-file hashes are retained in vendor/hayro-interpret/assets,
licenses/pdf-backend and ATTRIBUTION.md. These are existing reader dependency assets;
applications retain their own document-font selection and licensing policy.

Compact ICC Profiles by Clinton Ingram (CC0-1.0), and dependency CMaps (BSD-3-Clause).
Their licences and per-file hashes are retained in vendor/hayro-interpret/assets,
licenses/pdf-backend and ATTRIBUTION.md. These are existing reader dependency assets;
applications retain their own document-font selection and licensing policy.

Source provenance

The SVG icon preparation in crates/ui is adapted from:
- PhotoCraft, crates/ui-egui/src/icons.rs, revision e7a83ca342cdff568254f85f442b9cc8afb08066.
  https://github.com/storytold/photocraft
  Copyright (c) 2026 ArtCraft Team and the PhotoCraft contributors.
- VectorCraft, crates/ui-egui/src/icons.rs, revision 825d4fdb8b527c597855d273fb4bcc1971855b6a.
  https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft
  Copyright (c) 2026 ArtCraft Team and the VectorCraft contributors.
The icon-button interaction/style boundary is adapted from PhotoCraft (above) and:
- PdfCraft, crates/ui-egui/src/icons.rs, revision f626db25cca2c89f8fa3f7e30d22bf59faea65ec.
  https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft
  Copyright (c) 2026 ArtCraft Team and the PdfCraft contributors.
The tab fitting in crates/ui/src/tabs is adapted from PhotoCraft's tab_strip.rs (above).
Tab interaction adapters also use VectorCraft's dock.rs and floating.rs (above).
The pane sizing and resize boundaries in crates/ui/src/layout draw on:
- FilmCraft, crates/ui-egui/src/dock.rs, revision 7b6c134472287db4367fca80bcb498240ba36567.
  https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft
  Copyright (c) 2026 ArtCraft Team and the FilmCraft contributors.
- EffectCraft, crates/ui-egui/src/dock.rs, revision 2a460986ee7a4b32656a3d434849693904b486bc.
  https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft
  Copyright (c) 2026 ArtCraft Team and the EffectCraft contributors.
The widget-state styling in crates/ui/src/theme is adapted from VectorCraft (above),
crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs, and:
- DesignCraft, crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs, revision 66c7ce7e96ec286a091878cc2541ee8369aa79d6.
  https://github.com/storytold/designcraft
  Copyright (c) 2026 ArtCraft Team and the DesignCraft contributors.
The transactional panel model and drop-zone semantics in crates/ui/src/docking draw on the
FilmCraft/EffectCraft split, tab and accordion layouts and VectorCraft floating groups listed
above. The generic transaction validation, optional renderer and workspace-location helpers
are implemented here without dependencies on application engines or native window helpers.
All sources listed above are licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. No icon artwork is copied here.

The PDF spooler in crates/print is extracted from:
- PdfCraft, crates/print/src/spool.rs, windows_print.ps1 and spooler tests,
  revision 33c14e07cfd742a82bf03baa6b103c01008fa68c.
  https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft
  Copyright (c) 2026 ArtCraft Team and the PdfCraft contributors.
  Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. PDF composition and application code are not copied.

The Windows printer duplex-capability query and parser additionally draw on PdfCraft,
crates/print/src/spool.rs, revision fb97ce958dfe92b6762ce40615c7836551710139 (PR #1154), under the same licenses above.

The native Windows backend (crates/print/src/windows.rs, ticket.rs and the printer-list and
Windows spooler tests) is ported from PdfCraft's native printing work, which carries the
approach of PdfCraft PR #599 (Win32 printer list, Windows.Data.Pdf into the XPS print API, the
PrintTicket and its driver-paper preference):
- PdfCraft, crates/print/src/spool/windows.rs, spool.rs and tests.rs, branch
  claude/native-windows-print-826c99 of PR #1132, revision a435117 (jcl-bit/printcraft).
  https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft
  Copyright (c) 2026 ArtCraft Team and the PdfCraft contributors.
  Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0.

The colour management module in crates/cms is extracted from:
- PhotoCraft, crates/cms, revision b3222ee8e7e6bcb4799c37f904c595f20f9baf5e.
  https://github.com/storytold/photocraft
  Copyright (c) 2026 ArtCraft Team and the PhotoCraft contributors.
  Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. Its generated ICC profile is dedicated to the public domain
  (CC0-1.0); see ATTRIBUTION.md.

Optional PDF writer

Krilla 0.8.2 (https://github.com/LaurenzV/krilla), MIT OR Apache-2.0.
Upstream licence texts are retained in licenses/pdf-writer.
The optional writer embeds Compact ICC Profiles by Clinton Ingram
(https://github.com/saucecontrol/Compact-ICC-Profiles), under CC0-1.0.
See licenses/pdf-writer/LICENSE-ICC.txt and ATTRIBUTION.md for sources and hashes.
The writer adds no font files. Its four existing ICC profiles are retained under vendor/krilla/icc.

Krilla is vendored with a native unwind-cleanup patch; see vendor/krilla/README.craft.md
and vendor/krilla/SOURCE.json. Its upstream MIT/Apache-2.0 licences and CC0 profiles are unchanged.

Optional PDF reader

Hayro 0.7.1, hayro-interpret 0.7.0, hayro-syntax 0.7.2 and hayro-jbig2 0.3.0
(https://github.com/LaurenzV/hayro), MIT OR Apache-2.0, retain their upstream licence files.
These patched sources are transferred from PdfCraft revision
7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a (https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft).
See vendor/README.craft-reader.md and each crate's SOURCE.json for provenance and local changes.
The reader retains the existing Foxit/PDFium standard-14 font assets (BSD-3-Clause),
Compact ICC Profiles by Clinton Ingram (CC0-1.0), and dependency CMaps (BSD-3-Clause).
Their licences and per-file hashes are retained in vendor/hayro-interpret/assets,
licenses/pdf-backend and ATTRIBUTION.md. These are existing reader dependency assets;
applications retain their own document-font selection and licensing policy.

Third-party material

This product bundles third-party material under its own licenses, listed below. The per-file
list (author, source, license) is in ASSETS.md.

- Lucide icons (assets/icons/*.svg except dc-*.svg) — ISC License; the icons Lucide derived from Feather are also under the MIT License (Cole Bemis). See assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt.
- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.
- Inter (assets/fonts/Inter-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-Inter.txt.
- JetBrains Mono (assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-JetBrainsMono.txt.
- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

compiled into the app through the hayro-cmap crate under the BSD 3-Clause License:

The Husqvarna Viking HUS layout, its decompression (crates/sf-formats/src/hus.rs) and its thread
palette (sf_core::threads::hus_chart) are adapted from pyembroidery's HusReader.py,
EmbCompress.py and EmbThreadHus.py (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License.

The Janome SEW layout (crates/sf-formats/src/sew.rs) follows pyembroidery's SewReader.py
(https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License, and libembroidery's readSew and writeSew.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0

(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,

web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

Third-party material

This product bundles third-party material under its own licenses, listed below. The per-file
list (author, source, license) is in ASSETS.md.

- Lucide icons (assets/icons/*.svg except dc-*.svg) — ISC License; the icons Lucide derived from Feather are also under the MIT License (Cole Bemis). See assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt.
- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.
- Inter (assets/fonts/Inter-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-Inter.txt.
- JetBrains Mono (assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-JetBrainsMono.txt.
- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

Third-party material

This product bundles third-party material under its own licenses, listed below. The per-file
list (author, source, license) is in ASSETS.md.

- Lucide icons (assets/icons/*.svg except dc-*.svg) — ISC License; the icons Lucide derived from Feather are also under the MIT License (Cole Bemis). See assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt.
- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.
- Inter (assets/fonts/Inter-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-Inter.txt.
- JetBrains Mono (assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-JetBrainsMono.txt.
- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

# Code

ttf-parser
Code from ttf-parser was used/adapted for the following parts:
- Reader, Writer, LazyArray16 and LazyArray16Iter
- `name` table parsing.
- `hmtx` table parsing.

such as `calc_subroutine_bias`, `SIDMetadata`, `CIDMetadata` `RealNumber`,
`Index`, `IndexSize`, `OffsetSize`, `FDSelect`, `ArgumentStack`, `Top Dict` and `FONT Dict`,

Third-party material

This product bundles third-party material under its own licenses, listed below. The per-file
list (author, source, license) is in ASSETS.md.

- Lucide icons (assets/icons/*.svg except dc-*.svg) — ISC License; the icons Lucide derived from Feather are also under the MIT License (Cole Bemis). See assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt.
- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.
- Inter (assets/fonts/Inter-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-Inter.txt.
- JetBrains Mono (assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-JetBrainsMono.txt.
- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.
- Inter (assets/fonts/Inter-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-Inter.txt.
- JetBrains Mono (assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-JetBrainsMono.txt.
- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from

BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the

through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,

Third-party material

This product bundles third-party material under its own licenses, listed below. The per-file
list (author, source, license) is in ASSETS.md.

- Lucide icons (assets/icons/*.svg except dc-*.svg) — ISC License; the icons Lucide derived from Feather are also under the MIT License (Cole Bemis). See assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt.
- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.
- Inter (assets/fonts/Inter-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-Inter.txt.
- JetBrains Mono (assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-JetBrainsMono.txt.
- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

Third-party material

This product bundles third-party material under its own licenses, listed below. The per-file
list (author, source, license) is in ASSETS.md.

- Lucide icons (assets/icons/*.svg except dc-*.svg) — ISC License; the icons Lucide derived from Feather are also under the MIT License (Cole Bemis). See assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt.
- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.
- Inter (assets/fonts/Inter-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-Inter.txt.
- JetBrains Mono (assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-*.ttf) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-JetBrainsMono.txt.
- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,

web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

- Lucide icons (assets/icons/*.svg except dc-*.svg) — ISC License; the icons Lucide derived from Feather are also under the MIT License (Cole Bemis). See assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt.
- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.

- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

PDF import decodes CJK text with Adobe's CMap resources (https://github.com/adobe-type-tools/cmap-resources),
compiled into the app through the hayro-cmap crate under the BSD 3-Clause License:

-------------------------------

font is embedded by this dependency and no font file is added to this repo.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0

(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from

BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,

Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

This product bundles third-party material under its own licenses, listed below. The per-file

- Lucide icons (assets/icons/*.svg except dc-*.svg) — ISC License; the icons Lucide derived from Feather are also under the MIT License (Cole Bemis). See assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt.
- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.

- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

Linux Wayland window decorations
-------------------------------
sctk-adwaita 0.10.1 (https://github.com/PolyMeilex/sctk-adwaita,

for vector window controls. Its title-font features are disabled: no Cantarell
font is embedded by this dependency and no font file is added to this repo.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0

(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from

in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,

Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

- Lucide icons (assets/icons/*.svg except dc-*.svg) — ISC License; the icons Lucide derived from Feather are also under the MIT License (Cole Bemis). See assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt.
- Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 (assets/fonts/Source*) — SIL Open Font License 1.1. See assets/fonts/OFL-SourceSans3.txt, OFL-SourceSerif4.txt.

- Brother PEC, Janome JEF and Janome SEW thread palettes (crates/sf-core/src/threads.rs, `pec_chart`,
  `jef_chart` and `sew_chart`): the palette tables published in pyembroidery by Tatarize
  (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License; its notice is at the end of this file.
- egui's default fonts, compiled into the app through the epaint_default_fonts crate — Ubuntu Light
  (Ubuntu Font Licence 1.0), Hack (MIT), Noto Emoji (SIL Open Font License 1.1) and emoji-icon-font
  (MIT). Their license texts ship with that crate.

The photo cut-out code in crates/sf-photo (Select Subject, GrabCut, maximum flow, Gaussian mixtures,
SLIC superpixels, guided-filter edge refinement, distance transform, live-wire) is adapted from
PhotoCraft (https://github.com/storytold/photocraft, commit 04d0212) by the ArtCraft Team, under the MIT
License or the Apache License, Version 2.0, the same as this product.

The desktop app opens DWG drawings with acadrust (https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust, version
0.6.4), copyright its authors, under the Mozilla Public License 2.0
(https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/). It is used unmodified, as a library, through crates/sf-dwg; its
source code is available from that repository and from crates.io
(https://crates.io/crates/acadrust/0.6.4). The web app doesn't include it.

Builds made with the `heif` feature (not the official ones, for now) decode HEIC photos with heic-rs
(https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs, MIT OR Apache-2.0), through crates/sf-heif, adapted from
PhotoCraft's HEIF wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0). HEVC, the compression HEIC uses, is covered by patents
in some countries; whoever distributes such a build is responsible for any licence they need.

Rust dependencies (vello_cpu, kurbo, peniko, skrifa, harfrust, usvg, linesweeper, egui, eframe, …) are
fetched through crates.io under their own permissive licenses (mostly MIT and/or Apache-2.0; also
BSD, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 and Unicode-3.0).

JPEG export uses the jpeg-encoder crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, and the IJG License): this software is
based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

WebAssembly plug-ins run in the wasmi interpreter (MIT OR Apache-2.0); its wasmparser dependency is
under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM exception.

The experimental Windows 7 build (packaging/windows/windows7.ps1) compiles a modified copy of the
windows-link crate 0.2.1 (vendor/windows-link; Microsoft, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that binds CoTaskMemFree
through ole32.dll. Its license texts are in vendor/windows-link and ship in that build's ZIP; every
other build uses the unmodified crate from crates.io.

Builds made with the StitchFoundry fonts (the STITCHFOUNDRY_FONTS_DIR build option; all official
releases) embed the Foundry embroidery fonts of https://github.com/Stitchwright/stitchfoundry-fonts
(Foundry Block, Varsity, Script, Slab and Sans, digitized from Anton, Graduate, Pacifico, Alfa Slab
One and Open Sans), under the SIL Open Font License 1.1; their license texts ship with the release
packages as OFL-<folder>.txt and are shown in the app's font list.

Builds made with craft-fonts (the CRAFT_FONTS_DIR build option; all official releases) embed the
fonts listed in https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md (BIZ UDPGothic,
Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC and Noto Sans Arabic in the current manifest;
web builds BIZ UDPGothic Regular only) under the SIL
Open Font License 1.1. Their license texts ship with the release packages as OFL-<family>.txt.

EmbCompress.py and EmbThreadHus.py (https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License.

The Janome SEW layout (crates/sf-formats/src/sew.rs) follows pyembroidery's SewReader.py
(https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery), MIT License, and libembroidery's readSew and writeSew.
The Pfaff VIP reader (crates/sf-formats/src/vip.rs) follows libembroidery's readVip and carries its
colour key table: libembroidery (https://github.com/Embroidermodder/libembroidery), copyright
2018-2025 The Embroidermodder Team and Josh Varga, under the zlib/libpng License: "This software is
provided 'as-is', without any express or implied warranty. In no event will the authors be held
liable for any damages arising from the use of this software. Permission is granted to anyone to
use this software for any purpose, including commercial applications, and to alter it and
redistribute it freely, subject to the following restrictions: 1. The origin of this software must
not be misrepresented; you must not claim that you wrote the original software. If you use this
software in a product, an acknowledgment in the product documentation would be appreciated but is
not required. 2. Altered source versions must be plainly marked as such, and must not be
misrepresented as being the original software. 3. This notice may not be removed or altered from
any source distribution."

The Brother PEC and Janome JEF thread palettes come from pyembroidery
(https://github.com/EmbroidePy/pyembroidery, version 1.5.1, by Tatarize), under the MIT License:

Shared PDF backend

The patched hayro-interpret 0.7.0, hayro-syntax 0.7.2 and hayro-jbig2 0.3.0
are fetched from https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs at revision
ca50d63b773c99f96e75c77ce5a1d21e7c9cda0d. Their upstream project is
https://github.com/LaurenzV/hayro, licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. The snapshot retains each
crate's upstream licence files. The patch ledger is at
https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/blob/ca50d63b773c99f96e75c77ce5a1d21e7c9cda0d/vendor/README.craft-reader.md.

Linux Wayland window decorations
-------------------------------
sctk-adwaita 0.10.1 (https://github.com/PolyMeilex/sctk-adwaita,
commit d5f343c45c04d4a026db57f76760819b7325db00) is used by winit on Linux
for vector window controls. Its title-font features are disabled: no Cantarell
font is embedded by this dependency and no font file is added to this repo.
